page_title: Introducing Google Customer Reliability Engineering | Google Cloud Blog

summary.name: Google Customer Reliability Engineering (CRE)
summary.one_liner: A 2016 Google Cloud blog announcement of Customer Reliability Engineering (CRE), a program that applies Site Reliability Engineering practices to customers' production applications on Google Cloud.
use_cases: Understanding how Google applies SRE principles to customer applications
Evaluating reliability gaps in a critical cloud application
Learning the error budget concept for uptime targets
Designing a shared on-call and incident process with a cloud provider
Reading about cloud customer support philosophy
summary.what_it_does: The post introduces CRE as a Google Cloud role created to share operational fate between Google and customers. Google CRE engineers inspect a customer's critical application's code, design, implementation and operational procedures, and run it through a Production Readiness Review. The result is a list of reliability gaps and an error budget, plus recommended changes to reach more nines. Google also builds common monitoring so both sides share telemetry for paging and tickets. Listed benefits include shared paging, auto-created and escalated Priority 1 tickets, CRE participation in customer war rooms, and a Google-reviewed design. The author describes the SRE error budget concept (for example, 99.9% availability allows about 43 minutes of downtime per 30-day month) as background.
notable: Shared operational fate: Google engineers share pagers and escalation with the customer's team
Production Readiness Review applied to customer applications
Listed at $0 additional cost, but requires sustained customer effort; Google can 'hand back the pagers' if the customer does not participate
Explains the SRE error budget concept as background
caveats: Requires a strict review process and sustained commitment from the customer's own teams
Author states the program will not suit most customers, as the effort is significant
Describes a 2016 program announcement; current availability and terms are not stated on the page
